title: fix(plugin-form): hand a section's `description` to the drawer arm's two dividers
body:
Fixes #9834

Clause-②: no

`FormSection.description` is already declared on both sides — `DrawerFormSectionConfig.description` in this file's own props type and `FormSection.description` in `@objectstack/spec` — `ObjectForm`'s drawer map already copies it, and `SectionDivider` (the component the row renders as) has always drawn one. Making the drawer's own pushes read it relaxes no accepted set and enlarges no public surface. Re-declared here by me rather than inherited: I checked the two declarations myself.

Merge base I computed and branched from, ⛔ not one handed to me: `177d3799f9b655fc4867901b2a6372b9cf0e5d72` (`test(plugin-grid,console): pin the members of object-grid's four toolbar keys (objectui#8071 slice 13)`). The changeset-presence gate independently prints the same merge base.

## What was wrong, and which layer it was

`object-form` rendered as `formType: 'drawer'` dropped its sections' `description` — one layer LATER than the default layout did:

- `ObjectForm`'s drawer section map copies `description: s.description` onto the drawer's section config. That half worked.
- `DrawerForm`'s OWN explicit-sections `section-divider` push rebuilt the row key by key — `label`, the ADR-0089 predicate, the objectui#6236 membership claim, the collapse pair — and not `description`.
- Its derived-fieldGroups divider push did not carry it either, although `deriveFieldGroupSections` copies a declared group's `description` onto the section it emits.

So the author wrote the key, the first layer passed it, the last layer did not take it. The sibling member `label` arrived in the same call, which is what made the miss invisible.

**What I changed, stated as finished facts I controlled:** I made both of `DrawerForm`'s divider pushes read `description`, and I did not touch either push's gate. ⛔ I am deliberately not writing any sentence of the form "N arms render it now" — that is a live claim about a tree I stop controlling the moment this merges.

## ⛔ The gate was not widened — and one consequence that follows anyway

The derived push keeps its heading condition exactly as it was, so a derived group with no heading still draws no divider and still drops its blurb. That condition also decides the ADR-0089 predicate row and the objectui#6236 membership claim that gates the whole group, so widening it is a ruling about other keys (objectui#9835), ⛔ not mine to take.

⚠️ The explicit-sections push has a different starting shape, and this is worth reading rather than assuming: it was **already unconditional** — it pushes a divider row for every section, spelling the heading `section.label || ''`. `SectionDivider` itself renders nothing when it has neither a label nor a description. ⇒ once the key is copied, a drawer section carrying a `description` and no heading renders the blurb alone, where the same member on the default layout draws no divider at all. That falls out of copying the key, ⛔ not out of touching a gate, and it is pinned as a reading (row 5 of the new pin) rather than left to be rediscovered.

## The escalation condition, which I went and tested

The triage comment pre-wrote it: a THIRD layout arm also failing at its last layer would mean this is a general shape of the divider push rather than two coincidences. I read the last layer of every other arm AND measured each one through the real renderer (throwaway probe, two sections each carrying `label` plus a distinctive blurb, mounted through `ObjectForm` per `formType`; probe deleted, not in this diff).

| arm | last layer that receives the key | measured |
|---|---|---|
| `tabbed` | `TabbedForm`'s `tabGroups` carries `description: section.description`, out as `fieldTabs[].description` | blurb renders |
| `wizard` | `FormSectionContainer`'s own `description` prop, fed `currentSection.description` | blurb renders, current step only, which is the wizard's whole shape |
| `split` | `paneFields`' divider push carries `description: section.description`, gated `section.label || section.description` | blurb renders |
| `modal` | the stacked divider push carries `description: g.description`, gated `g.title || g.description`; the `contentLayout: 'tabbed'` sub-arm carries `fieldTabs[].description` | blurb renders |
| `drawer` | both of `DrawerForm`'s own pushes — the defect this PR repairs | blurb renders after this change; ⛔ did not before, shown failing below |

⇒ **No third layout ARM is affected**, so I proceeded with the two-push repair plus the pin, as dispatched.

⚠️ **But one reading goes back to the seat, because it speaks to the RATIONALE behind that condition rather than its letter.** A third divider push does not take the key, and it is not on a third arm — it is the MODAL arm's derived-fieldGroups fallback, the route a modal form takes when the host passes no `sections` and the object's own metadata declares `fieldGroups`. Measured, same instrument, on the tree with this PR applied:

```
PROBE modal-derived   heading_Money=true  blurb=false
PROBE drawer-derived  heading_Money=true  blurb=true
PROBE default-derived heading_Money=true  blurb=true
```

The modal arm renders the blurb on the authored-sections route an author normally reaches, so the ARM is healthy in the sense the card's table measures; its derived fallback is a separate push with the same shape the drawer's two had. Whether that satisfies "a third arm" and re-grades this family is the triage seat's call. ⛔ I did not decide it, ⛔ did not fix that push (it is another arm and outside this card), and ⛔ filed nothing — it is handed back in my report with dedupe words.

## The pin, and it is shown failing without the fix

The drawer arm's behaviour here was watched by **nothing**. It now has its own file, `drawerFormSectionDescription-9834`, deliberately separate from `objectFormSectionMembers-8071` — that file states its own scope in words as "the default layout only", and this is a different site that lost the same key one layer later.

Five rows: both routes a host can take into `DrawerForm` (through the real `ObjectForm` with `formType: 'drawer'`, and mounted directly — ⛔ neither a hand-built stub of the divider), the derived-fieldGroups push, an absence control so the instrument is one that CAN report none, and the ungated-push reading above. Every row reads the blurb off the divider row itself, ⛔ not off `document.body.textContent`, which any stray render of the same string would satisfy; every row carries the sibling `label` on the same section in the same call as its live control.

Ablation, run from the committed state so both legs are byte-provable, with a `trap` restoring on any exit:

- HEAD blob of the renderer: `4b68447d584cae41c0f452e09a9a16121d033e3a`, equal to the on-disk blob before the mutation — so the mutation started from HEAD, not from a dirty tree.
- Mutation = delete both copied keys. Landed on disk, proven by the anchor count going 2 to 0 (⛔ not by the editor's exit code) and by the mutated blob hashing `e5c3770c12d800fe017aa12a31b298331af7042a`, different from HEAD's.
- ⚠️ The first spelling of that mutation script asserted zero anchors and refused to run, because the ten-space anchor is a substring of the twelve-space one and `count` returned 2 for both. It failed loudly and changed nothing; I corrected the anchor to include the preceding newline rather than retrying until something landed.
- **Mutated leg:** `Tests 4 failed | 1 passed (5)`. The four reds are rows 1, 2, 3 and 5; the one green is row 4, the absence control, which is exactly the row that SHOULD stay green when the key is gone.
- **Restore leg:** `git checkout HEAD --` on the file (⛔ not a bare `git checkout --`, which restores from the index). Restored blob `4b68447d584cae41c0f452e09a9a16121d033e3a`, equal to HEAD's; `git diff HEAD` empty; anchor count back to 2; pin green again at `Tests 5 passed (5)`.

No build was needed for either leg and none was used: the pin imports `../DrawerForm` and `../ObjectForm` relatively, so it reads the mutated source directly.

## Prose this change makes false, corrected here

- `objectFormSectionMembers-8071`, row 7's comment, said a member with a blurb and no heading gets a divider from "four of the other arms (`split` / `modal` / `wizard` / `tabbed`)". Once the drawer's already-unconditional push copies the key, that count is wrong. Rewritten to state what THIS layout does and to point at each arm's own site and pin instead of carrying a count nothing re-derives.
- The same file's SCOPE paragraph now names `drawerFormSectionDescription-9834` among the neighbouring files that own per-arm facts, so a reader is not left thinking this key is watched in one place. Its stale "two neighbouring files" opener, which then listed four, is repaired while I am in the file.
- `registry-inputs-spec-parity`'s member-pin ledger entry for `object-form.sections` describes the behaviour being repaired. The file is INHERITED by this card — a card whose behaviour is pinned inherits that ledger whether or not its own fix touches it — and its entry is corrected in the same change, plus-one minus-one, exactly as the sibling card's did. That test still passes. No published behaviour of `@object-ui/console` changes.

Mechanical sweep for other carriers: the whole `packages/plugin-form` suite is green on the fixed tree, so nothing else in the package asserted the drop; a tree-wide search for prose claiming an arm count on this key returns exactly the one carrier repaired above, and the two other files that mention `DrawerForm` alongside `description` were read individually and are about the dialog's accessible description, not a section blurb.

## Changeset

Owed and a real bump, ⛔ not an empty-frontmatter declaration: `packages/plugin-form/src/DrawerForm.tsx` is published source of a released package. `@object-ui/plugin-form` patch. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` prints its own verdict line naming the declaration.

## Tests

Every heavy run went through the container's shared verify lock under one stable slot name, and each verdict below is that wrapper's own `VERDICT command-exit` line, ⛔ never a bare exit status read through a pipe.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/drawerFormSectionDescription-9834.test.tsx` at the merge base, BEFORE the fix — `Tests 4 failed | 1 passed (5)`, the reproduction both routes the card names, each red on the blurb with its heading control green.
- The same file after the fix — `Tests 5 passed (5)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/ apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` on the final tree — `Test Files 98 passed (98)`, `Tests 1124 passed | 1 skipped (1125)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form type-check` — exit 0; it runs `tsc --noEmit` AND `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new pin is type-checked too. The copied key needs no cast: `DrawerFormSectionConfig.description` is declared, so a rename would be caught by the compiler.
- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-form^...' build` — exit 0 (the dependency closure; the package cannot typecheck its own build against unbuilt dependencies).
- Gates, each captured to a file BEFORE any pipe: `check:changeset-presence`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:self-import` — all exit 0. `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the five changed paths prints NOT GOVERNED.
- A control-character self-scan over the five changed files finds none.

**Lint — a DECLARED narrowing, with the three things that make it a measurement rather than a skipped run.** Run at `cde5555d1c`, the final commit:

1. **Population, read from eslint's own config, not guessed:** `eslint.config.js` lints `**/*.{ts,tsx}` and carries exactly one `ignores` block, whose entries are build output (`**/dist`, `**/.next`, `**/node_modules`, `**/public`, `**/.source`, plus three literal generated artefacts). The repo-wide run is therefore every tracked TypeScript source, and it belongs to CI.
2. **What I ran, counted from the instrument's own output:** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the four changed source files reports `files linted: 4`, **0 errors**, 29 warnings. The warnings are all `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`: 24 pre-existing in `DrawerForm.tsx` (my diff adds no `any` to it — the added lines contain none), 2 pre-existing in the 8071 pin, and 3 in the new pin, which is the same `as any` idiom on a schema literal that the neighbouring pins use.
3. **Invariance over untouched files:** type-aware linting is NOT enabled anywhere in `eslint.config.js` — it declares no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, a grep for either returns zero — so no rule's verdict on a file this branch does not touch can depend on this branch.

⇒ the narrowing excluded nothing; the repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run, not one I owe.

## Acceptance notes

- Draft, as dispatched. ⛔ Not flipped ready, ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ no label applied — this repo's `needs:contract-review` label object exists but nothing reads it, and Clause-② is declared in this body, which is what the changeset check reads.
- Serial constraint: the inherited ledger file was declared free at claim time, and this PR touches it by one line as the card foresaw.
- Out of scope, ⛔ not filed, handed back in my report: the modal arm's derived-fieldGroups divider push drops this same key (measured above); and the boundary asymmetry between the drawer's unconditional push and the default layout's gated one, which is now pinned on both sides but has never been ruled on.
- ⛔ I took no arm count from any card body, this one included. Every arm reading above is one I measured on this tree.
